discovery: Rydberg blockade and programmable Rydberg-atom arrays for quantum simulation and quantum computation

nominees.name: Antoine Browaeys
nominees.affiliation: Institut d'Optique, CNRS, Université Paris-Saclay, France

subfield: Atomic, molecular and optical physics / quantum simulation
motivation: The nominees turned the strong, long-range interaction between Rydberg atoms into a controllable quantum resource. In 2009 Saffman's and Browaeys' groups (with Grangier) first observed the Rydberg blockade between two individually trapped atoms, and Saffman demonstrated the first neutral-atom CNOT gate. Browaeys and Lukin then developed defect-free, reconfigurable arrays of hundreds of optical tweezers, creating programmable quantum simulators of spin models. These platforms revealed new physics: quantum phase transitions in large Rydberg arrays, quantum many-body scars, and topological spin liquids. Lukin's group went on to demonstrate high-fidelity parallel gates and logical qubits with error-correction codes. Together these experiments established neutral atoms as a leading platform for quantum science and technology. They also opened a subfield that joins atomic physics, condensed-matter physics and quantum information.
